title: Snap tries to make the case again for its $2,200 smart glasses
snippet: Since Specs' debut earlier this year, Snap has clearly been looking for an opportunity to explain why the smart glasses deserve to exist.
fullText:
When Snap debuted its long-awaited smart glasses, Specs, earlier this year, the reveal was not only underwhelming but also a genuine disaster. The glasses — which cost a whopping $2,200 and are vaguely reminiscent of scuba gear — inspired jeers online and calls for the company’s CEO, Evan Spiegel, to resign. The company’s stock subsequently nosedived.

Since then, Snap has clearly been looking for an opportunity to explain why Specs — a heavy, expensive piece of hardware that most casual consumers will probably be unable to afford — deserves to exist. 

This week, the company had its chance to make that argument. At an event in Los Angeles, Spiegel and other Snap executives unveiled a variety of new features and services connected to Specs. The new updates seem clearly designed to help integrate the glasses into a broader array of digital activities and, in doing so, give Specs a clearer sense of purpose.

Image Credits:Snap (screenshot)

During Wednesday’s event, Spiegel shared details about a number of the new features. After a trippy promotional video that vaguely brought to mind an ayahuasca hallucination, the CEO took the stage and began a series of live demos.

New entertainment options — Specs can now connect with HBO Max and Spotify — provide a baseline of interactive fun that smart glasses have largely lacked until now.

Yet perhaps the biggest announcement was the launch of Specs Intelligence, which the company calls a new “anticipatory AI” system designed to pair not only with the company’s glasses but also with user devices — including iPhones and Macs. Snap claims that this new system “builds an understanding of your goals, priorities, relationships, and routines from the apps and tools you choose to connect, helping you focus on what matters now while making progress towards your longer-term goals.”

Image Credits:Snap (screenshot)

Spiegel called this system an “AI native operating system with intelligence designed around your projects” that helps users “connect the dots across Lenses,” Snap’s term for its AR camera effects, available on both phones and Specs, “so you can get things done while focusing on what matters to you.” In practice, it seems to function more like an AI productivity app that can be used with Snap’s glasses but doesn’t require them.

Snap has also announced a new program called Specs for Enterprise, which allows the device to be integrated into corporate workflows. On Wednesday, the company announced partnerships with a number of different tech companies — including Amazon, Salesforce, Nvidia, and other firms — in an effort to make the device useful to staff at those companies.

What is the real-world utility of this, and who is this service really for? Apparently, the answer is IT technicians. While the actual scenarios in which Specs can be used are a little vague, a demo video played at the event showed an IT technician repairing some hardware with the help of Snap’s new glasses.

“We’re building out mobile device management, security controls, and ways to deploy and manage stacks across teams with the world’s most trusted providers, bringing peace of mind to IT departments,” Spiegel said.  

Other announced features were slightly more head-scratching. For instance, one of the new experiences is an app, developed through a partnership with the NBA and WNBA, that allows users to practice basketball and improve their shot via the glasses’ AR capabilities. But, realistically, who is really going to play basketball while wearing heavy goggles on their head?

Also announced Wednesday was a new connectivity package for anyone who wants to use Specs on the go, away from Wi-Fi — like outside the home or office. Sold separately, the package includes a charging case with built-in cellular connectivity. That connectivity, which is being made available via a partnership with Verizon, costs $10 a month for Verizon customers and $20 a month for non-Verizon customers.

Spiegel ultimately framed Specs as a new way to engage with computing in a more human-centric format. “I will say it’s an interesting time to be launching a new computer because things in tech are pretty weird right now,” Spiegel said. “We’re being told that AI will take our jobs, that virtual worlds will replace the real one. Well, no, thank you. We do not accept that future. Making people irrelevant is not progress, and computers should make us more important, not less.”

Snap has repeatedly justified the product’s cringe-inducing cost by characterizing the device as a computer — albeit one you wear on your face. Whether consumers will go for that or not remains to be seen. The company has announced that it is hosting a Specs pop-up in Los Angeles in October before the devices ultimately ship later this fall.

title: GM’s New Software Plays Nice With Apple CarPlay, Android Auto
snippet: The 2027 Chevy Silverado and GMC Sierra fold phone mirroring into the native UI rather than walling it off, even as GM keeps Apple and Google’s apps out of its electric lineup.
fullText:
General Motors showcased a host of updates to its dashboard infotainment suite for its latest-generation pickup trucks this week. The new software includes a revamped home screen layout that can display more info more flexibly, deeper integration with the automaker’s Super Cruise highway-driving assist tech and a new, less bolted-on way to interact with Android Auto and Apple CarPlay. The combustion-powered 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500 pickups will be the first to get this new tech.

GM has offered CarPlay and Android Auto on its gas-powered vehicles for years, but has recently taken a different tack with its electric cars and trucks. The automaker pulled the phone-mirroring technologies from its EVs back in 2023, nudging owners toward its onboard Google Built-In software suite instead. 

GM CEO Mary Barra told journalists last year that Apple CarPlay or Android Auto would likely be phased out of its portfolio by 2028. The news that development of Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity has continued suggests that GM hasn’t totally walked away from the tech. But while we can continue to hope, that doesn’t mean mirroring is returning to the automaker’s EV lineup, either. What it does suggest is that GM thinks that internal combustion engine and battery electric vehicles require different tech tacks:

The new split-view home screen can display Apple CarPlay alongside native features, such as this trailer view.General Motors

“Customers should see a consistent GM foundation across our vehicles, but not an identical experience,” Sebastian Bauer, GM’s executive director of Human Interface Design, said in an internal interview shared alongside the announcement. “On top of that foundation, each brand and vehicle type should express its own character and personality.”

I reached out to General Motors for comment on the future of CarPlay and Android Auto in its EVs and was told, “We don’t have any additional updates to share at this time regarding the future availability of phone projection in GM EVs.”

The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500 will bring the tightest integration yet between the automaker’s native software and Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Rather than treating phone-mirroring technologies as separate modes that take over the entire screen when connected, CarPlay and Android Auto content will now appear in a split-view panel alongside native features like trailering data and vehicle status. 

In a blog post announcing the tech, GM says that drivers will be able to “seamlessly move between the two experiences, taking advantage of the features developed specifically for their truck and their device.”

In addition to the new software, the pickups will also get updated hardware with sharper displays and darker blacks.General Motors

The touchscreen infotainment in the 2027 Sierra and Silverado features a redesigned home screen with a new split-view layout that can be reconfigured to show a large map, trailering and fuel-efficiency data and media sources. In a blog post, the automaker says the new setup means drivers will be able to “browse audio and manage vehicle details without ever losing sight of your navigation.” 

The new split-view home screen and dashboard interface brings the same multitasking prowess to the onboard navigation software, audio and media sources. The automaker has also tweaked its one-tap “quick access” control window to be more customizable and easier to reach, and redesigned the incoming call and message notifications to be less intrusive. 

GM is also bringing deeper dashboard integration with its Super Cruise highway-driving assist. This hands-off, eyes-on driver assistance system enables the vehicle to steer itself on supported highway segments and is one of my favorite technologies in the automaker’s portfolio. 

Android Auto is handled similarly by the split-view home screen.General Motors

In the new 1500s, Super Cruise (and Adaptive Cruise Control on vehicles without the top-tier system) can now be engaged with a single button press, streamlining the process for the driver. An updated digital instrument cluster now features new dynamic views that automatically adjust when Super Cruising, trailering or going off-road. There’s also a new “3D driving visualization” view that lets the driver see what the vehicle sees (surrounding vehicles, lane markings and other objects on the road) in real-time.

The new UI is built as a single software platform across GM’s gas, diesel and electric powertrains, though not every vehicle that gets the tech will get an identical feature set. (EVs and phone mirroring being the most obvious example, but also vehicles not targeted at trails and towing may not get those dynamic views.) The automaker says the new infotainment suite will expand beyond trucks over time, with continuous over-the-air updates adding features after launch.

							Senior Writer, Electrified Cars

title: Lukewarm orders for iPhone 18 Pro, says analyst – but it doesn’t mean much
snippet: A high-profile analyst has said that demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max appears “lukewarm” based on pre-order wait times. Jeff Pu notes that most iPhone 18 Pro configurations are available for immediate delivery and that the longest wait for the most popular iPhone 18 Pro Max extends only to three to four weeks … more…
fullText:
A high-profile analyst has said that demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max appears “lukewarm” based on pre-order wait times.

Jeff Pu notes that most iPhone 18 Pro configurations are available for immediate delivery and that the longest wait for the most popular iPhone 18 Pro Max extends only to three to four weeks … 

Pu says that there’s no delay with most iPhone 18 Pro configs, while availability varies for the Pro Max:

Silver 1TB & 2TB models: Immediate

Black/Glacier 1TB: 1-2 weeks

Burgundy 1TB: 3-4 weeks

256GB and 512GB models in most colors: 3-4 weeks

Assuming consistent supply levels, this would indicate that the iPhone 18 Pro is less popular than most of its predecessors. However, there are so many caveats to this that our take is longer than reporting the data …

9to5Mac’s Take

Actual sales data for Apple products is, of course, extremely commercially sensitive, and the company long stopped revealing unit sales even in earnings reports. There are a number of ways analysts and market intelligence companies can try to get a steer on approximate numbers, however.

The most obvious of these is to look at estimated shipping times for new products. This is a very crude metric as what it actually measures is the gap between supply and demand. A million people wanting a new device and a million devices being stockpiled would still equal immediate delivery, while demand for 100,000 units with only 10,000 in stock would mean lengthy wait times.

Market intelligence companies do use other methods to supplement this. A common one is to use pre-recruited consumer panels who have consented to their inboxes being scanned for order emails. Consumer surveys are also sometimes used. A combination of methods can improve reliability, but ultimately it all amounts to educated guesses.

The huge variable this time around, as Pu himself acknowledges, is that we are still waiting for pre-orders to open for the iPhone Duo. An unknown number of those who would otherwise have ordered one of the iPhone 18 Pro models will be waiting for that instead. “Lukewarm” demand for the iPhone 18 Pro could potentially point to higher than expected demand for the iPhone Duo.

Things will get even more complicated once pre-orders do open for the Duo, since reporting has suggested that production yields have been relatively low, meaning that even modest demand could see lengthy waits for shipping.

title: Tim Cook keeping John Ternus away from controversy by attending White House dinner
snippet: One of the trickier parts of Tim Cook’s job when he was Apple CEO was walking the tightrope of upholding the company’s values without provoking the ire of the White House over things like immigration policy and DEI. His new role as executive chairman sees him retain responsibility for government liaison, offering replacement CEO John Ternus some degree of protection … more…
fullText:
One of the trickier parts of Tim Cook’s job when he was Apple CEO was walking the tightrope of upholding the company’s values without provoking the ire of the White House over things like immigration policy and DEI.

His new role as executive chairman sees him retain responsibility for government liaison, offering replacement CEO John Ternus some degree of protection … 

Past challenges

The challenges Cook faced in the past date back many years. For example, back in 2018, changes to US immigration policy and practice affected thousands of Apple employees. Tim Cook was among a number of CEOs who wrote to the administration stating that the changes were causing “considerable anxiety for many thousands of Apple employees,” as well as “threatening to disrupt company operations.”

Cook faced similar difficulties last year when Trump said that Apple should get rid of its DEI policies. He responded by saying the company would comply with any changes to the law but would not compromise its values.

Cook is now Apple’s official diplomat

Earlier this year, Apple confirmed that Cook’s new role includes responsibility for liaising with governments.

As executive chairman, Cook will assist with certain aspects of the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world.

Attending White House dinner next week

Bloomberg reports that Cook will be attending a White House state dinner for China’s president next week. The event takes place at a difficult time for US-China relations, especially over AI.

Apple Inc. Executive Chairman Tim Cook and OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman are poised to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping next week […] The summit comes at a delicate moment for US-Chinese relations — and the artificial intelligence industry. Geopolitical tensions are simmering over the AI race, international trade and the Middle East.

9to5Mac’s Take

I would wager a large sum of money that the idea of the diplomatic role being Cook’s responsibility came from the man himself. It’s a self-sacrificing move intended to free his successor from unnecessary distractions and controversies.

Ternus will of course still be constrained in what he can say when it comes to Apple’s response to controversial policies and laws, whether in the US, China or elsewhere, but having official responses be the responsibility of someone else does give him more latitude than would otherwise be the case.

title: iOS 27.2 references new option to overwrite iPhone storage with blank data after erasing
snippet: Apple is working on a new option to more thoroughly wipe an iPhone’s storage when erasing the device, but there’s a catch. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple is working on a new option to more thoroughly wipe an iPhone’s storage when erasing the device, but there’s a catch. Here are the details.

New feature exclusive to Chinese devices

References included in today’s iOS 27.2 beta 1 point to a new iPhone erasing option that will let the user overwrite the device’s entire storage with blank data, including storage that isn’t actively in use.

In addition to erasing the iPhone’s data, the feature can overwrite the device’s entire storage with blank data, including storage that isn’t actively in use. Apple warns that the process may take longer than a standard erase and could affect the device’s lifespan.

The move is interesting, as currently, when a user erases an iPhone, the device’s encryption keys are destroyed, effectively rendering the remaining data inaccessible. In fact, Apple is very clear about this in an Apple Platform Deployment support article:

On the device, erasing (or wiping) obliterates all the keys in effaceable storage and renders all user data cryptographically inaccessible.

While digging through today’s beta, 9to5Mac confirmed that, as currently implemented, the feature will only be available on iPhone models sold in China, where Apple appears to be adding it to comply with an upcoming data-erasure requirement.

That’s because a new Chinese standard taking effect on January 1, 2027, will require smartphones and other electronic devices to offer a way to more thoroughly erase stored data, including through methods such as overwriting it.

For semiconductor storage, such as the flash storage used in smartphones, one approved method involves overwriting storage containing user data at least once with meaningless data. That closely matches Apple’s description of replacing storage with blank data.

Finally, the new erasing option won’t be exclusive to iPhones, as code references also point to support for other devices, including the iPad, HomePod, and Apple Vision Pro.

fullText:
Apple has a new beta cycle beginning today, and it’s a surprising one: rather than the iPadOS 27.1 update we were expecting, iPadOS 27.2 beta 1 is now here.

Apple releases iPadOS 27.2 beta 1 for testing, skipping over iPadOS 27.1

iPadOS 27 launched this week to all users, and now Apple has skipped right over 27.1 for beta testers and has released iPadOS 27.2 developer beta 1 instead.

It’s unclear why today’s update isn’t designated 27.1. But so far, the one thing we know about iOS 27.1 is that it will ship with iPhone Duo.

Perhaps Apple plans to keep 27.1 focused exclusively on iPhone Duo-related changes? In any case, we’re interested to see what kind of new features iPadOS 27.2 might bring.

Shortly before iPadOS 27 shipped, Apple removed the ‘Suggestions’ feature that had previously been available in Messages, as well as the Passwords app option to have compromised logins agentically replaced with secure new logins.

Apple hasn’t said when those features will return, but it’s possible we’ll see them in today’s beta.

Another possibility is the redesigned Health app, which Apple said will arrive later this year with new AI enhancements.

fullText:
Walmart has the best deals in Google TV with its Onn series and, right now, a relatively wide restock has brought the Onn 4K Pro back for many not long after Google TV Streamer saw a pretty major price hike.

title: X and SpaceXAI move to drop Apple from antitrust lawsuit, keep claims against OpenAI
snippet: X and SpaceXAI today filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss their claims against Apple in the antitrust lawsuit they brought against the company and OpenAI. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
X and SpaceXAI today filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss their claims against Apple in the antitrust lawsuit they brought against the company and OpenAI. Here are the details.

Claims against Apple dropped, pending court approval

Last year, Elon Musk accused Apple and OpenAI of colluding to keep competing AI apps from gaining visibility on the App Store.

Soon after, X and xAI (now, SpaceXAI) filed an antitrust lawsuit against both companies, arguing that Apple’s agreement to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence gave OpenAI an unfair advantage over rival AI services. Both companies disputed all claims.

Since then, the case has moved into discovery, with the parties fighting over access to internal documents and communications.

A few months ago, a federal judge ordered Musk to turn over potentially relevant emails from his Tesla and SpaceX accounts after OpenAI argued that he had used those accounts to conduct xAI business.

Today, X and SpaceXAI filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss with prejudice their claims against Apple, while keeping their claims against OpenAI.

From the filing:

Plaintiffs have resolved their claims in this Action against Defendant Apple Inc. (“Apple”).

Plaintiffs accordingly move under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 41(a)(2) to dismiss with prejudice their claims against Apple. Apple does not oppose this Motion.

For the avoidance of doubt, Plaintiffs do not seek to dismiss any of their claims against Defendants OpenAl Foundation (f/k/a OpenAl, Inc.); OpenAl, L.L.C.; and OpenAI OpCo, LLC.

Since X and SpaceXAI moved to dismiss with prejudice their claims against Apple, this means that X and SpaceXAI don’t intend to bring those same claims against Apple again in the future. It is worth mentioning that the dismissal is not final yet, as Judge Mark Pittman still needs to approve it.

As for OpenAI, the case now looks somewhat like a spiritual successor to Musk’s separate lawsuit against the company, Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and Microsoft, which ended earlier this year.

In that case, Musk accused OpenAI of abandoning the nonprofit mission under which it was founded and improperly enriching its executives at his expense. A jury ultimately rejected Musk’s claims in May, finding that they had been filed too late.⁠

title: iOS 27 adds three new iPhone features you’ll use all the time
snippet: iOS 27 launched this week as a major iPhone update, here are three new features that could be among the most-used for many users. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 launched this week as a major iPhone update, here are three new features that could be among the most-used for many users.

#1: Siri AI

Whatever your opinion of Siri has been in the past, iOS 27’s Siri AI is different.

Siri didn’t just get an AI glow-up with a few upgrades. Apple says it “tore [Siri] to the ground” and “rebuilt it from the ground up.”

You can now ask Siri about anything, like you might ask Google or ChatGPT, and it provides informed, helpful answers. It can also perform way more actions on your iPhone than before, and works seamlessly and consistently across all your devices. There’s also a dedicated Siri app to hold all your conversations.

I’ve been using iOS 27’s new Siri for three full months, and it’s became a daily go-to for me.

#2: Automatic proofreading, including for grammar

The iPhone has long offered a basic spellcheck feature that underlines any words it identifies as misspelled. Now in iOS 27, Apple is expanding proofreading in two ways:

spellcheck is now powered by Apple Intelligence  

there’s a new tool for checking grammar

AI being applied to spellcheck means even if a word is technically spelled correctly, you’ll see suggested word replacements if your iPhone thinks the word is being used incorrectly.

Whereas misspellings are typically underlined in red, suggested word replacements and grammar issues are underlined in blue. Compared to common typos, this makes them feel more like optional suggestions rather than in-your-face warning signs.

If you’re not a fan, you can always disable proofreading in Settings. But I’d guess that for lots of users, these features will be welcome iOS 27 additions.

#3: Search overhaul in Spotlight, Photos, and Mail

Search is one of the most essential features for most apps, and certainly for the iPhone as a whole. And in iOS 27, Spotlight search has received a major overhaul.

In addition to having Siri fully integrated with Spotlight, the iPhone’s systemwide search has been rebuilt with a more comprehensive index of your content that always stays up to date throughout the day.

This means you should find Spotlight more useful than ever, as it offers better and more relevant results with every search. Apple says that the same new search foundation powering Spotlight has been implemented in the Photos and Mail apps too, upgrading search across those key apps. So far in my testing, I can very much tell the difference.

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8 fix 200+ vulnerabilities
snippet: If you’re on the fence about installing macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple’s lengthy list of security fixes might be enough to convince you. And if you’re sticking with an older version, you may want to install macOS Tahoe 26.7 or macOS Sequoia 15.8 sooner rather than later. Here’s why. more…
fullText:
If you’re on the fence about installing macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple’s lengthy list of security fixes might be enough to convince you. And if you’re sticking with an older version, you may want to install macOS Tahoe 26.7 or macOS Sequoia 15.8 sooner rather than later. Here’s why.

Apple fixes 200+ macOS vulnerabilities

Apple today published the full security changelogs for macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8, detailing more than 200 vulnerabilities addressed in the updates.

As has been the case with several recent macOS updates, Apple’s acknowledgments include multiple AI-focused security teams and researchers, including OpenAI Codex Security, NVIDIA AI Red Team, and Anthropic Research.

Fixes included in macOS 27 address vulnerabilities that could allow malicious apps or attackers to execute arbitrary code with kernel or root privileges, escape the macOS sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper protections, modify protected system files, access sensitive user data, and more.

One AVEVideoEncoder flaw, for instance, could allow a sandboxed app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges. Meanwhile, a UDF file system vulnerability could similarly allow an app to execute code at the kernel level. Apple also fixed vulnerabilities that could lead to remote code execution through Bluetooth, CUPS, and WebDAV.

As for macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8, the updates patch many of the same vulnerabilities, including several kernel-level, root-privilege, sandbox-escape, Gatekeeper-bypass, and remote-code-execution flaws listed above.

The older systems also feature some additional fixes not listed for macOS 27, including an ImageIO vulnerability in macOS Sequoia 15.8 that could allow arbitrary code execution when processing a maliciously crafted image.

title: Apple’s Health App Hits Developer Beta. I Got the Inside Scoop From Apple’s VP of Health and Fitness
snippet: From readiness, longevity and AI insights to blood tests and movement assessments, we covered everything about the Health app’s redesign.
fullText:
Last week at Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” event, Dr. Sumbul Desai, Apple’s VP of Health and Fitness, announced the redesigned Health app and its fresh features. Between the new Insights tab with Apple Intelligence-powered suggestions, a Longevity tab that shows your Health Age, a readiness score, movement assessments, a blood panel and curated doctor videos, my head was swimming with questions. The following day, I sat down for a video chat with Desai for deeper insight into Apple’s reimagined health platform.

Now, on Wednesday, the new Health app debuted in the first developer beta of iOS 27.2. Some announced features will be available in later betas, including personalized summaries under the Insights tab, personalized recommendations and the ability to order a blood panel from Quest Diagnostics. 

“Features will roll out progressively,” Apple said in an email. “Feedback during the beta period will help us continue refining it ahead of the public release in late 2026.”

Here’s everything you can expect to uncover in the Health app and the features you shouldn’t sleep on.

From data spreadsheet to intelligent experience

Launched in 2014, the Health app was initially intended to be like a spreadsheet, with data flowing in, Desai explained. However, the team realized they wanted more from the app, so it evolved over the past 12 years into what Desai now calls “an experience.”

Those at the helm of the Health app’s 2026 makeover considered how to leverage Apple’s machine learning and AI to help people live healthier, while also personalizing the app’s recommendations and turning it into an intelligent hub, not unlike the iPhone itself. For instance, as you open the app and move through your day, different screens appear to reflect your health status. 

Movement assessments have also been added to provide an even more complete picture of a user’s health and track progress or decline. Desai described them as a “mini physical” you can complete at home.

All assessments under the app’s Longevity tab are science-based and contribute to a rainbow-petal visual that illuminates your state of health. Some assessments rely on vision-based AI models that integrate the phone’s camera, marking the first time Apple has used the camera for health.  

The current iteration of the Health app is just the beginning and was designed to set in motion the next era of the team’s work in health and fitness, as Desai said those working on the app still feel they have more to do.

The Longevity tab’s rainbow visual.Apple

Health Age: Biological vs. birthday

One standout feature from Apple’s event was the Health app’s Longevity tab, which will include a feature called Health Age that uses health metrics such as your VO2 max (the maximum amount of oxygen your body consumes during exercise), resting heart rate, sleep and heart rate variability, along with lab data such as LDL cholesterol and A1c for your average blood sugar level, to provide your biological age, which represents how your body is aging on a cellular level when compared to your actual age. 

Apple’s own Heart and Movement Study, which it applies across all its health products, informs both Health Age and Readiness, which uses your activity data, daytime and overnight vitals and sleep data to tell you about your capacity for the day ahead. 

The five-year Heart and Movement Study was conducted in collaboration with the American Heart Association and Brigham and Women’s Hospital to explore the connection between heart health and physical activity. Apple used that data to create the normative ranges for the insights it provides in the app.

While Desai acknowledged the Health Age assessment is more of a “fun way to look at your health habits” and that no one can tell you your actual biological age, it’s another way to provide insight and suggest healthy habits users can integrate into their lives. 

I’m also hoping my Health Age is lower than my actual age. Apple

Apple’s secret sauce

Apple isn’t the first company to offer features such as a readiness score or biological age, but Desai said that it stands out from competitors because of its unique perspectives, experiences and the science behind its work. 

“When we first started our work in health, when we announced our irregular heart rhythm notifications and ECG, those were clinically validated scientific features,” she said. Desai likened those early days to building a muscle that lets the team create impactful products the medical community will appreciate, and users can easily understand.

That muscle Apple first built has been exercised with all the Health app’s new features, as Desai said that everything is rooted in science. On her team, for instance, physical therapists graded each movement in the app’s mobility assessments to ensure that when a movement is picked up and a result is given, it’s graded the way an actual physical therapist would grade it. 

Uniting science and expertise, Desai said that’s what Apple brings to the table, and its Health app experience. 

The new Health app’s ‘sleeper hit’

Much of the discourse following Apple’s event has been about the new readiness score and Health Age. I was curious what Desai felt was the “sleeper hit” feature that didn’t get as much attention. 

“It’s actually the assessments,” Desai said. “You’re going to be able to, on a regular basis, do a push-up test and a core test and see if you’re improving. Then we give you insights and things that you can do to improve, and then you can test again. It’s almost like having a physical therapist or a trainer.”

The VO2 max test, in particular, marks the first time Apple’s doing an on-demand, in-the-moment VO2 max test. 

You can then take all your assessment results, and the Health app will put them into a report you can share with your doctor. 

A person performing a movement assessment using their iPhone.Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Homing in on your body’s big players

Based on its new assessments, the Longevity tab’s visualization has seven tabs: heart health, sleep, mental wellbeing, movement health, metabolic health, hearing and nutrition. But how did Apple narrow it down to those seven?

“We picked areas where we felt like we had the appropriate data to comment on,” Desai explained. “For example, we do a cardiovascular risk score through some of the questions. It’s based on traditional risk scores and cardiovascular risk scores that are done.”

The team prioritized information they believe people will use and assessments they’ll complete, while ensuring the chosen health areas feel holistic and will help people concerned about long-term quality of life.

“There’s still more that we think we can do, but this is where we’re starting,” Desai stated. In other words, Longevity’s rainbow visual could gain more colors in the future. 

Keeping privacy at Apple’s core

When it comes to its Health app, Desai said privacy is where they start and end. 

“Candidly, we may not always be the first to market, but when we release something, we can stand behind it from a privacy standpoint,” Desai stated. “All the features you saw [announced] are no different. … It’s part of the conversation every day, and up till the day that the products are launched.”

Apple will hold off on releasing a product if it hasn’t met its privacy bar. The team behind the Health app also uses a checks-and-balances system, having other teams review their work to ensure they are nailing their privacy approach. 

“In this world where more things happen in the cloud, we want to make sure that’s all encrypted and private, which is why we have Private Cloud Compute,” said Desai. Private Cloud Compute is Apple’s cloud intelligence system designed for private AI processing.

The team’s approach is end-to-end because privacy matters for all your data, not just health data. 

Apple Intelligence has suggestions

The Health app’s new Insights tab uses Apple Intelligence to analyze your health metrics and provide a timely summary that updates throughout the day. 

“We also make suggestions,” said Desai. “For example, if you have an injury or you’re trying to work on your mobility, we’ll give you suggestions on the types of exercises you might be doing.”

It’s another example of how the app is evolving from a database to something that more closely resembles a personalized health advisor.

The daily insights are meant to be bite-size pieces of information that are one small thing you can do for your health each day. Some days these insights may be interesting; other days, you might be given information you already know.

Under Insights, the For You section will use your data to offer personalized recommendations and relevant articles.Apple

Health on a cellular level, explained

For $119, the new Health app will let you purchase a blood panel with over 50 biomarkers through Quest Diagnostics. You can also get your blood pressure, height, weight and waist and hip circumferences measured. All this helps provide a more complete picture of metabolic health.

The revamped app will include videos from doctors that help people better understand what they see in the app. 

“When you get your assessment results, you’ll actually see your own data in the videos where they’re explained by clinicians,” said Desai. “We have a physician, a physical therapist, a sleep expert, a mental health expert. The reason we did that is, for certain things, gamification works, but for certain things, you just want to know the information in an easy-to-understand way from an authoritative resource.”

While an expert explains the subject at hand, your health data, whether from your labs or your Apple Watch, will be overlaid on the video so you can see it as you learn more. 

Ultimately, Desai doesn’t see the future of the Health app as one size fits all. Depending on the feature, the team always chooses what makes health as accessible and understandable as possible. In a world with an abundance of health data, perhaps that’s what matters most: ensuring people understand the numbers they see on their devices, and knowing what to do with them once the screen goes black. 

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Anna Gragert
						

						

							Senior Editor, Health and Home						
					

											

								

											Anna Gragert (she/her/hers) was previously the lifestyle editor at HelloGiggles, the deputy editor at So Yummy and the senior lifestyle editor at Hunker. Over the past 12 years, Anna has also written for the LA Times, Elle, Bust Magazine, Dazed, Apartment Therapy, Well+Good and more. At CNET, she's a senior editor on the Healthy Home team, and her coverage includes health, wellness tech, meal kits and home and kitchen tech with a focus on the technology that aims to help us live our healthiest, happiest lives.

title: Spotify expands its partner program for podcasts to 35 new countries
snippet: Spotify said since changing its video podcasts creator terms in January, its payouts have increased by more than a third.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

5:00 AM PDT · September 17, 2026

Image Credits:Klaudia Radecka/NurPhoto (opens in a new window) / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

Spotify is expanding its partner program for podcasts, which lets podcasters earn money from ad and Premium revenue sharing, to a total of 35 regions, including Italy, Spain, Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, Poland, Chile, the Dominican Republic, and the Bahamas this fall.

Eligible podcasters will be able to earn revenue from both video and audio podcasts — video impressions by Premium users count toward revenue, as does ad revenue share from free users listening to the show. The company said podcasters can distribute their shows on other platforms and also keep all the revenue they earn from sponsorships.

Spotify has so far run its partner podcast program in the U.S., Europe, and Australia, and this is the streaming service’s biggest geographical expansion for this program.

The company said that video podcast consumption on Spotify has increased 140% since the feature was launched in 2022, and its total monthly payouts to shows has gone up a third since January.

Earlier this year, Spotify changed its eligibility criteria to earn revenue from video podcasts. Creators can now apply if they have a minimum of three episodes online, 2,000 consumption hours, and 1,000 engaged audience members for the last 30 days. The company said this change has increased consumption in participating shows by an average of 45%.

title: Cricket Wireless Adds 5G Home Internet Service
snippet: Cricket joins the club of mobile providers bundling home internet with mobile phone service.
fullText:
With 5G cellular speeds now fast enough to rival broadband, many mobile providers are asking: Why should you have separate services for your phone and home? Cricket Wireless is the latest company to answer with a new home internet service that rides the same 5G network you’d get while out with your mobile phone.

Cricket 5G Home Internet service by itself delivers unlimited data on AT&T’s 5G network for $60 per month (with Auto Pay enabled). It also requires purchasing a $50 Cricket Gateway modem.

Bundling a wireless line with home internet service costs $75 for new customers. However, the price drops to $45 per month if you’re an existing Cricket Wireless customer and add the home internet option.

The wireless Cricket Gateway creates a Wi-Fi network to serve your at-home devices and delivers download speeds up to 300Mbps and upload speeds up to 30Mbps. That can be throttled in rare cases, “if your usage is contributing to congestion on the network” for 30 minutes, according to Cricket. Speeds and availability depend on how good AT&T’s coverage is in your area.

Being a prepaid service, there’s no ongoing contract. And since the gateway is purchased, not rented or leased, stopping service means you’d have an extra box of technology lying around instead of dealing with the hassle of returning it.

It’s also nice to see Cricket include taxes in the prices, something many carriers now make additional fees.

Cricket’s 5G home internet service is available now.

							Senior Writer

title: Gears of War: E-Day and Minecraft Dungeons 2 Headline Xbox Game Pass September 2026 Additions
snippet: As Microsoft continues to reshape Game Pass, a new lineup of games is arriving for subscribers.
fullText:
Microsoft continues to modify its Xbox Game Pass service as the company tries to get a handle on how expensive it is. The company said that in November it will eliminate the unlimited cloud gaming perk that comes with a subscription and instead limit the number of hours based on the membership level. Rumors circulated on Monday claiming other changes were coming to the service, including the removal of Day 1 games, an ad-supported tier and a decrease in subscription costs. Microsoft didn’t confirm or deny the rumors, only saying it didn’t “have any changes to announce today or plans that have been finalized.”

September’s Xbox Game Pass lineup has some heavy hitters coming in at the end of the month and at the start of October. Gears of War: E-Day, a prequel to the series, is the biggest title coming to the Xbox platform before Grand Theft Auto 6‘s release on Nov. 19. Microsoft, like every other game publisher, hopes to get its big guns out before the gaming world is completely taken over by the next GTA game.

Xbox Game Pass, a CNET Editors’ Choice award pick, offers a wide selection of games you can play on your Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S, Xbox One and PC or mobile device for as little as $10 per month. With a subscription to the higher-tiered Game Pass Ultimate ($23 per month), you can access hundreds of games, including new ones the day they’re released, each month. 

Here are all the games Xbox is bringing to Game Pass in September.

RuneScape: Dragonwilds 

Game Pass Ultimate, Premium and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 15.

Dragons have returned to the forgotten land of Ashenfall, leaving players to survive in a dangerous new wilderness. Gather resources, craft equipment, build a home and develop your skills as you explore the continent and uncover the secrets behind the Dragon Queen.

Kernel Hearts

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 17.

This anime-style action RPG combines fast-paced combat with roguelike progression and optional co-op. Choose from four characters with distinct abilities and playstyles as you climb the Tower of Babel, developing your skills and learning more about your companions along the way.

Dune: Awakening 

Game Pass Ultimate, Premium and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 22.

Set on the harsh desert world of Arrakis, Dune: Awakening blends survival mechanics with open-world exploration and RPG elements. Gather resources, build your base, craft equipment and uncover a cinematic story as you attempt to survive on one of the most unforgiving planets in the universe.

Well Dweller

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 22.

This dark fairy tale adventure puts you in control of Glimmer, a tiny bird armed with nothing more than a matchstick. Explore a troubled kingdom, meet its unusual inhabitants, battle dangerous creatures and navigate a sprawling Metroidvania world as you try to save Glimmer’s family from a wicked queen.

Mad King Redemption 

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 23.

This 2.5D beat ’em up combines classic arcade-style fighting with roguelite progression, meaning each run offers something different. Fight through waves of corrupted enemies, build up your character and attempt to break the Mad King free from his growing insanity.

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Sept. 29.

This sequel sends players beyond the familiar Minecraft world and into the mysterious Sift. Team up with friends to battle new enemies, explore unfamiliar environments and collect gear that can be customized to suit your play style as you prepare for increasingly difficult challenges.

Gears of War: E-Day

Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass subscribers can play on Oct. 6.

Set 14 years before the original Gears of War, this prequel follows Marcus Fenix and Dominic Santiago as the Locust Horde launches its devastating first attack. The campaign explores the beginning of the conflict that would define the series, putting you in the middle of humanity’s fight for survival.

Other games coming to Xbox Game Pass

Those are some of the games Microsoft is bringing to Xbox Game Pass soon, but the company is adding more this month. Here are the other games you can try soon.

Marvel Cosmic Invasion: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 16. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Planet of Lana 2: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 16. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Routine: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 16. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Ultimate Sheep Raccoon: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 16. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Call of Duty: Black Ops 6: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Sept. 25. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Keeper: Coming to Game Pass Premium on Oct. 2. Previously on Game Pass Ultimate and PC Game Pass.

Games leaving Game Pass soon

While Microsoft is adding those games to different Game Pass tiers, the company is removing eight others on Sept. 30. You still have time to play these games for the first time, or finish your campaign, before you have to buy them separately, but you should hurry.

Atomfall

Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light

Little Nightmares 2 Enhanced Edition

Little Rocket Lab

Sifu

SOPA Tale of the Stolen Potato

Sworn

Terminull Brigade

title: Google Home app brings battery-efficient widget, reduces gray device tiles
snippet: Besides Home MCP, Google today is also rolling out Home app (especially for the homescreen widget) and Gemini for Home voice assistant updates. more…
fullText:
Besides Home MCP, Google today is also rolling out Home app (especially for the homescreen widget) and Gemini for Home voice assistant updates.

The Google Home widget has now been optimized to “pause background updates and polling whenever your phone’s screen is powered off, locked, or running a screensaver.” This helps save battery on your phone and connected cameras, while “ensuring your widgets refresh immediately the moment you unlock your phone.”

Meanwhile, Google has resolved an issue with device tiles for sensors, cameras, and smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. They could previously “appear grayed out after returning from device controller screens.” As such, you no longer have to reload the screen.

Other quality improvements include:

	

Smoother multi-account switching: If you have multiple accounts that you use with Google Home, switching between them is now more reliable with fewer “Home not found” errors and preference resets.

More reliable smart device setup: Addressed several setup and onboarding issues, including eliminating stalls during Wi-Fi pairing. This ensures a smoother, frustration-free onboarding journey when adding new smart devices to your home.

Smoother Google TV startup: Resolved a startup crash on Google TV devices, ensuring the Google Home experience launches reliably on your television.

More flexible in-app banners: Improved UI for triggering actions in announcement banners in the Google Home app.

Smoke alarm notifications: Rolling out improvements to smoke and carbon monoxide alarm notifications to show current device status in the Google Home app after an alarm has already been cleared.

On the camera front, there are three fixes:

Improved camera live stream tile reliability (Android): Resolved an issue where returning from the full-screen camera view back to the Favorites tab caused live stream tiles to temporarily turn black until manually scrolled. Live feeds now continue streaming seamlessly upon navigating back.

Smoother camera history scrolling across recording gaps (Android): Video timeline scrolling now smoothly scrolls past unrecorded or offline gaps without freezing.

Faster switching to live camera stream (iOS): Fixed an issue where tapping the “Live” button while watching recorded events failed to redirect smoothly into the live view, leaving playback paused.

Finally for September 16, 2026, Google has five Gemini for Home voice assistant updates:

Improved follow up question behavior: Minimized cases where Gemini asks unnecessary follow-up questions or ends conversations awkwardly.

Fixed TV streaming playback: Fixed an intermittent issue that prevented Gemini from launching TV streaming providers on smart displays.

Reduced Live Mode interruptions: Addressed an issue where some devices interrupted themselves during Live Mode.

Reduced Broadcast errors: Resolved an issue where there were error messages when attempting to broadcast. You can now more reliably broadcast across your whole Home.

Improved Playlist reliability: Fixed some issues where Gemini wasn’t able to identify and play personal playlists.

title: Apple Weather adds two convenient new features in iOS 27
snippet: Apple Weather adds two convenient features in iOS 27 that make it easier to track rain and wind forecasts. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple Weather adds two convenient features in iOS 27 that make it easier to track rain and wind forecasts. Here are the details.

iOS 27‘s Weather app adds rain and wind forecast views to home page

iOS 27 is packed with new features for Apple Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Messages, and more.

While Apple Weather is lighter on changes, there are two convenient additions worth noting:

Rain forecast view

Wind forecast view

Essentially, Apple has taken a bunch of data that was previously buried behind different menus and hidden screens and made it conveniently front and center.

We’re all familiar with the default forecast view in the Weather app. It’s one of the first things you see every time you open the app.

In iOS 27, Apple has split the forecast view into three options: Conditions, Precipitation, and Wind.

Conditions is the same view that was there before. But now, you can tap the new rain and wind icons to switch to Precipitation and Wind views.

When you hit each icon, both the hourly and 10-day forecasts instantly change.

The Precipitation view offers the chance of rain for each hour coming up, plus chances of rain with helpful measurements and time-of-day estimates for the next 10 days. Similarly, the Wind view shows the speed of gusts per hour, and ranges of what to expect in the days ahead.

I’ve been loving these changes during my time using iOS 27. They make key information more accessible than before while letting you stay in the familiar environment of the home screen.

title: Samsung reportedly rushing new trifold phone in response to iPhone Duo
snippet: It was already clear that Samsung was worried about the impact of the iPhone Duo on its foldable phone range, and there’s now further evidence of the Korean company’s concern. A blogger who aggregates reports from Chinese social media says there are signs that the company is bringing forward the launch of its Galaxy Z Trifold 2, despite the seeming failure of its predecessor … more…
fullText:
It was already clear that Samsung was worried about the impact of the iPhone Duo on its foldable phone range, and there’s now further evidence of the Korean company’s concern.

A blogger who aggregates reports from Chinese social media says there are signs that the company is bringing forward the launch of its Galaxy Z Trifold 2, despite the seeming failure of its predecessor …

Given Samsung’s poor track record on the robustness and reliability of its foldable phones, it’s not surprising that it felt threatened by the build quality of the iPhone Duo. Even before the new model was officially unveiled, the company was criticizing the reported weight of the device.

Once it was announced, it was clear that Apple had addressed a key weakness of Samsung’s foldables: vulnerability to damage caused by the ingress of dust and dirt. While Samsung’s latest folding model is only rated to IP48, leaving it vulnerable to particles as large as a grain of sand, the iPhone Duo is rated to IP68, meaning fully dustproof.

Samsung now appears to be hoping that if one fold isn’t enough, perhaps two will do the trick. Our sister site 9to5Google spotted a report suggesting Samsung plans to bring forward the launch of the Galaxy Z Trifold 2 in direct response to the iPhone Duo.

This would be a more surprising move given that the original dual-fold model wasn’t exactly a market or financial success.

The original TriFold made its US debut in January for $2,900 and was discontinued barely three months later [amid] rumors that it was sold at a loss.

Next year’s model is expected to sell for roughly the same price as the original.

title: MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro goes official with 2nm process and performance gains
snippet: MediaTek has unveiled its latest flagship chipset in the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a chip built on TSMC’s latest 2nm process. more…
fullText:
MediaTek has unveiled its latest flagship chipset in the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a chip built on TSMC’s latest 2nm process.

The Dimensity 9600 Pro has a 2+3+3 All Big Core CPU design using Arm’s new C2-Ultra cores at 4.55GHz, three C2-Pro cores at 4.35GHz, and three more C2-Pro cores at 3.1GHz. Altogether, MediaTek says that its latest design delivers 17% better single-core performance and 15% higher multi-core performance compared to last year’s chip. 

Leading where others follow, the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 is a first-wave 2nm smartphone chip design that’s built to simultaneously raise the bar on performance, capability, and power-efficiency…

At its heart is MediaTek’s 4th-generation All Big Core CPU: a revolutionary 2+3+3 design pairing two Arm C2-Ultra processors, three Arm C2-Pro processors with 1MB L2 cache and three Arm C2-Pro with 512KB L2 cache, which altogether contribute to a 21% larger L2 cache system.

…MediaTek leads the industry with first-wave support for both UFS 5.0, which delivers 2x faster read/writes than the previous generation, and LPDDR6, which boosts effective memory bandwidth by 33% at the same frequency.

This latest chip adopts LPDDR6 memory and UFS 5.0 storage. The G2-Ultra NX GPU brings a 27% boost to peak performance while hitting 24% lower power consumption. Ray-tracing is 18% faster and games support up to 185fps. 

On the AI side, Dimensity 9600 Pro’s second-gen Super Efficient NPU reduces power consumption by 40% while delivering better performance and higher token generation per watt. 

	

Rounding things out, the Imagiq 1290 ISP supports 4K240 native direct-output ultra-slow-motion video, 4K120 cinematic log, and AI-powered True Color Tone and 60fps motion capture features. 

One of the first devices powered by the Dimensity 9600 Pro will be Oppo’s Find X10 Pro Max, due to be announced next week. Meanwhile, MediaTek is also announcing the Dimensity 9600M as a lower-cost version of this chip with “flagship-level performance.” It lacks UFS 5.0 and uses Arm’s C1 cores instead of C2.

Apple may still be cleaning up after the end of the iPhone launch, but attention is already turning to an October event.

There are still a lot of new products we’re expecting the company to unveil, with the most exciting of these including touchscreen MacBooks and a smart home hub we’ve been dubbing the HomePad. But which ones will launch this year, and which ones will have to wait until next year … ?

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has laid out his latest expectations. He’s still being a little coy with exact timings, simply saying that some products will launch “later this year” rather than specifically in an October event. This year

Gurman says we can expect six new products later this year:

Touchscreen MacBook Pro models (likely in 14- and 16-inch versions)

An updated 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip (non-touchscreen model)

A new iMac, although this will only be new colors and an M6 processor

HomePod mini 2, with Siri AI

Apple TV 4K, with Siri AI

First half of 2027

The iPad Air is also expected to get an OLED screen for the first time, as well as a more powerful chip.

The rest of the list is lengthy, but mostly comprises iterative updates:

IPhone 18, mostly expected to be the iPhone 17 with A20 chip

IPhone 18e, likewise only seeing a chip upgrade

MacBook Air models with M6 chip

MacBook Neo with an A19 Pro chip

Entry-level iPad with Siri AI support

iPad Pro models with chip and cooling upgrades

Two Apple Pencil updates, both expected to be compatible with the iPhone Duo

Later in 2027

Things are, however, expected to get much more interesting in the second half of next year. 

Smart glasses; AirPods with built-in cameras; a home security system and related device; a redesigned Apple Watch; a 20th-anniversary iPhone line; and a second-generation iPhone Duo.

title: Apple files Supreme Court brief challenging contempt ruling in Epic case [U]
snippet: Apple today formalized its challenge to the contempt ruling in its long-running legal battle with Epic Games, filing its opening merits brief with the U.S. Supreme Court. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple today formalized its challenge to the contempt ruling in its long-running legal battle with Epic Games, filing its opening merits brief with the U.S. Supreme Court. Here are the details.

A bit of context

As 9to5Mac readers know, the Supreme Court recently accepted Apple’s request to review a contempt ruling in the lawsuit Epic Games brought against the company in 2020.

In a nutshell, although Apple came out on top on most of Epic Games’ claims in the original lawsuit, it lost on one key point, with the court finding that Apple’s anti-steering rules violated California’s Unfair Competition Law.

As a result, the court issued a permanent injunction requiring Apple to allow developers to include links and other calls to action that direct users to third-party payment options.

The order read:

Apple Inc. and its officers, agents, servants, employees, and any person in active concert or participation with them (“Apple”), are hereby permanently restrained and enjoined from prohibiting developers from (i) including in their apps and their metadata buttons, external links, or other calls to action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms, in addition to In-App Purchasing and (ii) communicating with customers through points of contact obtained voluntarily from customers through account registration within the app.

Apple changed its rules to allow those links, but imposed a commission of up to 27% on purchases made through them. When Epic challenged the company’s compliance plan, the court agreed with the Fortnite maker and held Apple in contempt for violating the injunction.

Today’s brief

In today’s brief, Apple notes that when it “filed its notice of compliance on January 16, 2024, the district court did not raise any immediate concern.”

Apple adds that Epic itself acknowledged that the injunction “did not explicitly prohibit” the company from charging a commission on purchases made outside the App Store. Still, Epic argued that the new commission and related rules violated the “spirit” of the injunction, and the district court agreed.

Since then, Apple has been trying to overturn the contempt finding, arguing that there was nothing in the original injunction that prohibited it from charging a commission. This is the ruling Apple is now asking the Supreme Court to reverse.

Today, Apple filed its official opening merits brief, laying out its case for why the contempt ruling should be overturned.

Apple argues that “civil contempt for violation of an order may not be imposed unless an order provides clear notice that the conduct at issue is proscribed,” and cites past court decisions to support its case that “a party may not be held in contempt unless an order leaves no fair ground of doubt that it prohibits the particular conduct at issue.”

From the filing:

When it comes to “contempt proceedings,” therefore, an order’s “terms” govern. Terminal R.R. Ass’n of St. Louis v. United States, 266 U.S. 17, 29 (1924). Only “a plain violation of the decree so read” can justify contempt. Id. And an alleged contemnor’s intent is irrelevant: ‘Since the purpose [of civil contempt] is remedial, it matters not with what intent the defendant did the prohibited act. McComb v. Jacksonville Paper Co., 336 U.S. 187, 191 (1949); see Taggart, 587 U.S. at 561. What matters is that the order giving rise to contempt afford clear notice to the parties. Needless to say, silence is not enough. See, e.g., Perez v. Danbury Hosp., 347 F.3d 419, 425 (2d Cir. 2003) (vacating contempt order resting on conduct as to which the court order was “silent”).

Apple also takes aim at the Ninth Circuit’s broader standard, arguing that it is an outlier in allowing parties to be held in contempt for violating the “spirit” of an injunction. According to Apple, that approach lets courts decide after the fact that conduct was prohibited even when the injunction itself never clearly said so.

Apple also argues that allowing the contempt finding to stand would increase the risk of judicial overreach when courts enforce injunctions:

That approach not only fails to afford parties the explicit notice this Court’s precedents require, but it also amplifies the unique risk of abuse threatened by the contempt power. Courts have the power to modify or clarify injunctions on a going-forward basis to address new or changed circumstances, but the severe remedy of contempt is limited to situations in which a party violates the unambiguous terms of an order.

With Apple’s opening merits brief now filed, Epic has until November 13 to file its response, with Apple’s reply due December 14. The case could then be heard by the Supreme Court as early as January 2027.

Apple filed their Supreme Court briefing today. Now Apple’s PR team has begun sharing its muddled talking points on the topic with the press as reflected in this confused article. Phil Schiller was much better at this. 😀

Epic is fighting for the right of all developers to give… https://t.co/JrVfJ2RV3I

title: macOS 27 Golden Gate now available, here is everything new
snippet: After months of beta testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to everyone, bringing Apple’s new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major Safari additions, and a long list of performance and quality-of-life improvements. Here’s everything new. more…
fullText:
After months of beta testing, macOS 27 Golden Gate is now rolling out to everyone, bringing Apple’s new Siri AI, deeper Liquid Glass refinements, major Safari additions, and a long list of performance and quality-of-life improvements. Here’s everything new.

During this year’s WWDC, Apple presented its operating systems somewhat differently than users and developers were used to.

Rather than introducing new features for each platform individually, Apple spent relatively little time on each operating system and focused much of the event on cross-platform features and improvements, largely because many of them rely on the new Apple Intelligence framework.

That said, macOS 27 Golden Gate still includes several welcome improvements of its own, both in design and functionality, starting with some much-needed tweaks to Liquid Glass.

Liquid Glass and UI improvements

While macOS Tahoe 26 featured Apple’s revamped look, it fell short visually compared to other systems, particularly iOS 26 and iPadOS 26.

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple spent some time further integrating the new Liquid Glass into the system, while also bringing over some of the visual tweaks introduced in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. That includes a new Liquid Glass slider, which lets users customize just how transparent or opaque they want the effect to be.

The Liquid Glass appearance setting also includes a fun little easter egg featuring Clarus the Dogcow, which appears when you scroll the demo pane all the way down, and then keep going.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also introduces revamped app icons, more in tune with the Liquid Glass look, with additional layers that add depth and detail across light, dark, tinted, and all-clear global system settings.

The same goes for the revamped traffic light buttons Apple introduced midway through the beta period. Rather than the old flat green, yellow, and red controls, they now feature a Liquid Glass look, complete with a playful bouncing effect when users click (or perhaps, soon, touch?) and drag them before letting go.

Another welcome interface improvement in macOS 27 Golden Gate is Apple’s decision to standardize the corner radius across system windows and apps, rather than making it dynamic based on the UI elements present in a window’s menu bar.

Although Apple’s intentions were deliberate, many assumed the inconsistent corner radii were a bug, prompting Apple to specifically call attention to the change during the WWDC keynote.

An equally divisive design decision Apple rolls back with macOS 27 Golden Gate is the sheer number of icons shown alongside menu items. With macOS 26 Tahoe, Apple added symbols next to nearly every command across its apps, an attempt to make menus more visually descriptive that instead drew criticism for making them busier and, in some cases, harder to scan.

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple has (thankfully) reversed course, removing most of those icons and returning menus to a cleaner, less visually cluttered look.

Other visual tidbits in macOS 27 Golden Gate include edge-to-edge sidebars and more distinct active windows, both of which were also divisive in macOS Tahoe 26.

Siri AI and the new Siri app

This is perhaps the most significant new feature of macOS 27 Golden Gate. Apple’s revamped Siri, developed in partnership with Google’s Gemini model, gets its own app, in addition to an in-depth, system-wide integration.

The new Siri AI leverages a new per-device indexing system for the user’s data and lives in both Spotlight and the new Siri app.

The Siri app looks and works just as users are mostly used to with other AI assistant apps: a left-hand panel lists the user’s chat history across all compatible platforms, while the main chat panel lets the user type in prompts, attach images and files, or dictate to start a voice-based conversation. The app also supports search and pinned conversations, which is a nice plus depending on the user’s workflow.

The new Siri AI can pull information from the web and the user’s context to provide useful, actionable answers. During the beta period, the new Siri received overwhelmingly positive feedback, even though it can sometimes be slower than users accustomed to other LLM-powered AI assistants expect.

Another useful ability of the new Siri AI is its ability to interact with native and third-party apps, in addition to taking actions directly, taking the app integration available with the old Siri significantly further.

Importantly, developers need to expose their apps’ content and capabilities through the App Intents framework, so expect this aspect of the new assistant to improve over time as more developers update their apps for macOS 27 Golden Gate.

Finally, there is a systemwide “Ask Siri” option in context menus that lets users select text, images, or files and ask Siri about them directly. For example, users can Control-click an image in a document and ask Siri to help them learn more about it, or select a portion of text and ask Siri to rewrite it, proofread it, change its tone, or provide feedback on the writing.

Siri AI is available in English at launch, with support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish coming in October. For now, Siri AI won’t be available in China or in the EU due to regulatory issues.

Apple Intelligence

We went in-depth on Apple’s new foundation models here, but the gist is that for its 2027 OS releases, the company developed a new version of its Apple Intelligence models. Here’s Apple on each one:

AFM 3 Core, the next generation of our 3-billion-parameter dense model that delivers a step up in quality.

AFM 3 Core Advanced, our most powerful on-device model. It’s natively multimodal, enabling helpful features like expressive voices and higher-accuracy dictation. Built on cutting-edge Apple research, this 20-billion-parameter model uses a sparse architecture, activating just 1 to 4 billion parameters at a time depending on the request. AFM 3 Core Advanced is unlocked by and optimized for our most capable Apple silicon systems.

AFM 3 Cloud, our server-side workhorse, optimized for speed, efficiency, and performance.

ADM 3 Cloud (Image), for image generation and editing, which unlocks advanced photo-editing tools, the all-new Image Playground, and more.

AFM 3 Cloud Pro, our most capable server-based model, which powers our most demanding use cases, like agentic tool use and complex reasoning.

In practice, macOS 27 Golden Gate leverages two local models, AFM 3 Core and AFM 3 Core Advanced, while the other models are cloud-based. The performance of these two local models depends on the Mac’s hardware, particularly how much memory it has available to run their active parameters and other AI workloads.

When it comes to how Apple Intelligence is implemented in macOS 27 Golden Gate, it is somewhat of a mixed bag. The models themselves are quite good for everyday tasks, such as getting help to draft an e-mail, proofreading a document, or summarizing text.

The problem is that Apple is currently going somewhat overboard on how and when Siri AI is presented to the user, which can sometimes be a bit overwhelming or get in the way of what the user is trying to accomplish.

One great Apple Intelligence addition to macOS 27 Golden Gate is a new Visual Intelligence shortcut. By pressing Command-Shift-Space, users can select any region of the display and immediately ask Siri about it. That works with images, PDFs, text, or just about anything else shown on screen.

Alas, not every macOS 27-compatible Mac will run the new Apple Intelligence, which requires an A18 Pro, M1, or later chip. Here’s Apple’s official list of Macs that support the new features:

MacBook Neo (2026)

MacBook Air with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

MacBook Pro with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

iMac with Apple silicon (2021 and later)

Mac mini with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

Mac Studio (2022 and later)

Mac Pro with Apple silicon (2023)

Most Apple Intelligence features are available in the same languages supported by the current version of Apple Intelligence, including Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

Apple Intelligence is currently unavailable in China due to regulatory issues. Additionally, Apple says there will be usage limits for certain Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features, although the company has yet to share specific details on that.

Performance and reliability improvements

During the WWDC26 keynote, Apple highlighted dozens upon dozens of improvements coming to all its operating systems.

On macOS 27 Golden Gate, this means faster AirDrop transfers, improved network file browsing, faster Spotlight indexing (particularly for shortcuts and actions), and faster iCloud Photos uploads with selective priority syncing.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also improves Safari and Calendar scrolling, as well as the animations in Mission Control and Spaces. Apple also tweaked Mail indexing and search, as well as the underlying system for Spotlight suggestions.

Other tidbits include improved window position consistency and persistence across external displays, HDR support for system UI elements, a broader range of high-resolution and high-refresh-rate modes for external monitors, and more complete touch support in Sidecar, including tapping controls, one-finger scrolling, system gestures, and Markup.

Safari

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces Notify Me, a new Safari feature that can monitor webpages and alert users to relevant changes, such as price drops, product restocks, event registrations opening, or virtually anything else they ask it to track.

Notify Me can check for changes hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly, with additional options to specify the days of the week and times when those checks should run.

Additionally, Safari on macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces “Describe an Extension,” which lets users create extensions using natural language.

To help users get started, Apple provides several examples across productivity, focus, creativity, and design and development. Users can also simply describe what they need in their own words and let Apple Intelligence handle the rest.

Both features can be accessed from the “More Options” hamburger menu on the right side of the active Safari tab.

For users who tend to open way too many tabs as the day progresses, Safari can now automatically organize and group tabs together based on topic.

Another interesting tidbit in Safari in macOS 27 Golden Gate is the new pull-to-refresh gesture, which, like on iOS and iPadOS, lets users refresh the page by swiping down past the rubber-band effect.

This gesture is also available in other system apps, such as Mail, News, and Calendar, which many see as further foreshadowing of touchscreen Macs rumored to be announced as early as this year.

iPhone Mirroring

With macOS 27 Golden Gate, users can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window to different aspect ratios, a change many saw as an early sign that Apple was preparing the feature for a foldable iPhone.

Well! You can now resize iPhone Mirroring to ANY size! (on an iOS 27-compiled app)

Foldable iPhone is so coming LOL

it doesn't switch to iPad layout though, which is weird… now I am scared for foldable iPhone pic.twitter.com/B9hjxuXWH5

— Dylan (@DylanMcD8) June 8, 2026

Now that the iPhone Duo is official, Mac users can get an early taste of what that experience will look like. Alas, Apple notes that iPhone Mirroring remains unavailable in the European Union.

Shortcuts

This is perhaps one of the most useful additions to Apple Intelligence in Apple’s OS updates this year.

Despite its relatively approachable take on automation, Shortcuts can still feel intimidating to more casual users. Now, users can simply describe what they want to accomplish, and Apple Intelligence will build it as a native shortcut.

To help users get started, the Shortcuts app also highlights several suggestions on the new shortcut creation screen, including:

Dictate and translate to Spanish

Write a weather forecast haiku

Play my exercise playlist when I arrive at the gym

Create a recipe from these leftovers

Summarize my day every morning

Prioritize my to-do list every morning

When I get in the car, get directions

Dictate my idea and save it to the clipboard

Dim screen brightness when Bedtime begins

Turn on Do Not Disturb when I open the TV app

As a side note, if you’d like to get deeper into Shortcuts, make sure to follow Stephen Robles’s fantastic work on YouTube and on Instagram. Also, check out Shortcuts Playground, from MacStories, an even more powerful natural-language-based shortcut creation tool.

Photos

The Photos app now offers three Apple Intelligence-powered editing tools: an enhanced version of Clean Up, which removes objects, people, or other undesired elements from photos; Extend, which generates the surrounding area of an image in case the user decides the original photo is too cropped-in; and Spatial Reframing, which lets users change the angle and composition of a photo after it has been taken.

Additionally, iCloud Shared Albums now supports full-resolution sharing and lets Windows and Android users join in via iCloud.com.

Other new features include playing any set of photos and videos as a slideshow with custom music, transition styles, and duration, photo ratings with a new star system, and a new, dedicated “Captured by Me” collection.

More macOS 27 Golden Gate tidbits

Calendar lets users add, edit, or update events by describing them.

Finder can now intelligently suggest file and folder names, based on their contents.

Image Playgrounds expands support for different styles, and leverages a new foundation model for even better results

Maps gets an enhanced Flyover experience with improved textures, more details, and sharper rendering for hundreds of cities around the world.

Messages now (finally) consolidates tapback notifications and improves syncing across devices.

*Notes supports trackpad-handwritten notes and sketches, expands Markdown support with copy/paste, and adds Section Links.

Podcasts now supports video podcasts, complete with support for picture and picture playback.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also marks the final release to support Rosetta. As Apple explains, “only apps will no longer run on Mac computers with Apple silicon after this update,” and you can read more about that here.

Compatibility

According to Apple’s official list, macOS 27 Golden Gate is compatible with the following Macs:

MacBook Neo (2026)

MacBook Air with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

MacBook Pro with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

iMac with Apple silicon (2021 and later)

Mac mini with Apple silicon (2020 and later)

Mac Studio (2022 and later)

Mac Pro with Apple silicon (2023)

Do you have a favorite new feature? Let us know in the comments.
